This step describes the labeling of single cell suspensions resulting from bone marrow differentiation (step 15 h.) for flow cytometry.Note: Two staining strategies are described. In the single-step approach, lineage exclusion is performed directly in the BUV737 channel, allowing all target populations to be labeled and analyzed within approximately 50 min (Advantage: Speed). In the two-step approach, biotinylated antibodies for combined lineage exclusion are incorporated in the primary incubation, while staining with backbone markers and streptavidin-BUV496 takes place in a second staining step. This frees the BUV737 channel for relocation of Siglec-H thus increasing flexibility in backbone panel design. Moreover, it avoids inclusion of two different states of the same BUV737 tandem dye in the same channel which would be incompatible with spectral flow cytometry (Advantages: Precise compensation and panel flexibility). Dependent on the cell numbers required for analysis, this protocol step can be flexibly scaled up or down. For scaling, keep a constant target (cell number) to detection (staining cocktail volume) ratio. steps.title: Euthanize and fix mouse
steps.instruction: Euthanize the mouse by cranial dislocation, confirm loss of reflexes, place the mouse ventral side up on the preparation table, extend the legs distally and fix the mouse by puncturing each paw with a 23‑gauge needle.

steps.title: Isolate hind‑leg bones
steps.instruction: Harvest tibias and femurs from the hind legs, remove skin and fur, dislocate femurs from the hip joint, cut off the hind legs, and store the bones on ice.

substeps.instruction: Fix hind legs to the table and cut the abdominal wall skin.
Open the ventral side with scissors, cutting from proximal to distal.
Remove the fixing needles.
Make a circular incision at the femur‑hip junction on each side and pull the skin proximally to expose the bones.
Dislocate femurs laterally from the hip joint (critical to preserve femur integrity).
Stretch the processed leg away from the hip, cut off the hind leg, and place the whole leg in an empty 6‑well plate on ice.
Remove feet by rotating them against their natural direction (fibula usually removed together) or cut them off with scissors.
Isolate tibias, remove fibulas, and keep bones on ice.
Trim away all muscles and soft tissue by cutting parallel to the bone without rupturing it; if feet were cut with scissors repeat the same for the lower leg.
Rub residual tissue off the bone with a gauze bandage or rugged paper wipes (apply pressure perpendicular to the bone).
Store cleaned femurs and tibias from the same donor in empty 6‑well plates on ice until all mice are processed.

steps.title: Flush bone marrow
steps.instruction: Extract marrow from tibias and femurs directly onto a 100 µm filter placed over a 50 mL tube using ice‑cold RPMI‑1640 + 2 % FBS, after a brief ethanol dip and opening of bone ends.

substeps.instruction: Dip each bone sequentially for 4–5 s in 70 % ethanol, then wash in PBS (skip if bone is ruptured).
Open both ends of each bone with scissors just enough to expose the marrow.
Attach a 27‑gauge needle to a 10 mL syringe filled with ice‑cold RPMI‑1640 + 2 % FBS and flush the marrow onto the filter; pool 5–6 mice if desired.

steps.title: Create single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Triturate the filtered marrow, bring the volume to 40 mL with ice‑cold RPMI‑1640 + 2 % FBS, and centrifuge at 700 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Use the plunger of a 3 mL syringe as a pestle to triturate the marrow on the filter.
Rinse the filter and pestle with 5 mL ice‑cold RPMI‑1640 + 2 % FBS.
Top up the tube to a total volume of 40 mL.
Centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C, brake and acceleration set to maximum.
Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Erythrocyte removal
steps.instruction: Choose either ACK lysis (fast, harsh) or Lympholyte‑M gradient (milder) to eliminate red blood cells.

substeps.instruction: If using ACK lysis:
• Resuspend pellet in 500 µL ACK lysis buffer per mouse (scale proportionally for pooled samples).
• Incubate 5 min at 18–22 °C (adjust time if viability issues arise).
• Stop lysis by adding 4 mL ice‑cold RPMI‑1640 + 2 % FBS and vortex.
• Pass the suspension through a 40 µm filter into a 15 mL conical tube, rinse filter with an additional 5 mL RPMI‑1640 + 2 % FBS.
• Centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant, dab tube on paper towel.
• Resuspend pellet in 1 mL FACS buffer, top up to 10 mL, take an aliquot for counting, then centrifuge again (700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C).
• Discard supernatant, dab dry, resuspend in FACS buffer to 1 × 10^8 cells / mL, proceed to antibody staining.
If using Lympholyte‑M gradient:
• Pass the suspension through a 40 µm filter into a 15 mL tube, rinse the tube with another 5 mL RPMI‑1640 + 2 % FBS and repeat filtration.
• Centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant, cap tube, spin again briefly to ensure the rotor reaches 700 × g, then stop.
• Remove remaining supernatant with a pipette.
• Resuspend cells in a minimum of 5 mL FBS‑free RPMI‑1640 (18–22 °C).
• Layer the suspension over an equal volume (≥5 mL) of Lympholyte‑M (pre‑inverted three times, equilibrated to 18–22 °C, protected from light).
• Centrifuge 1 000 × g for 20 min at 18–22 °C with brake off or at minimum setting.
• Collect the lymphocyte layer at the interface with a 10 mL pipette in one smooth motion.
• Transfer to a 15 mL tube, top up to 10 mL with ice‑cold RPMI‑1640, vortex 10–20 s.
• Centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 10 mL RPMI‑1640 + 2 % FBS.
• Take an aliquot for cell counting.

steps.title: Count cells with Neubauer chamber
steps.instruction: Determine cell concentration using an improved Neubauer counting chamber, applying the appropriate dilution factor and chamber constant.

substeps.instruction: Dilute an aliquot of the suspension as needed; record the pre‑dilution factor (f_pre‑dilution).
Load 10 µL of the diluted suspension into the chamber, counting at least two large 1 mm² squares (preferably the four corner squares).
Count 50–100 intact lymphocyte‑sized cells per large square; calculate average N_avg = total cells counted / number of large squares counted.
Use the chamber constant k = 10^4 mL⁻¹ to compute concentration: c (cells / mL) = N_avg × f_pre‑dilution × k.
If total cell number is required, multiply c by the total suspension volume.

steps.title: Prepare cells for DC differentiation
steps.instruction: Resuspend the counted bone‑marrow cells in DC differentiation medium to a final concentration of 2 × 10^6 cells / mL and keep on ice (pause point up to 3 h).

steps.title: Stain progenitor cells – primary antibody
steps.instruction: Label bone‑marrow single‑cell suspensions for myeloid progenitor analysis with the primary antibody cocktail (Table 3).

substeps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL (≈1 × 10^7 cells) per well into a 96‑well V‑bottom plate; keep on ice.
Prepare 100 µL of primary antibody cocktail per well using the dilutions listed in Table 3 (e.g., FcγRIV‑9E9 1:400, FcγRIIB/III‑931 1:200, CD3ε‑145‑2C11 1:200, etc.).
Add 100 µL cocktail to each well, vortex gently, and incubate 20 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant by inverting the plate and tapping on a paper towel.

steps.title: Stain progenitor cells – secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Apply the secondary antibody cocktail (Table 5), wash, and prepare cells for acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 60 µL ice‑cold FACS buffer.
Add 100 µL of secondary antibody cocktail per well (Table 5; e.g., BUV737‑Siglec‑H 1:200, BUV496‑Streptavidin 1:50, etc.).
Incubate 20 min at 4 °C in the dark; check for aggregates and resuspend if needed.
Top up with 60 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Resuspend in 160 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge again (700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C), discard supernatant.
Resuspend final pellet in 50 µL FACS buffer, keep on ice.
Add 100 µL DAPI working solution immediately before acquisition on a BD LSR Fortessa SORP.

steps.title: Stain differentiation cultures – single‑step
steps.instruction: Label cells from bone‑marrow‑derived DC cultures using a single‑step antibody cocktail (Table 8).

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge cells 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet to 1 × 10^6 cells / mL in FACS buffer.
Aliquot 100 µL per well of a 96‑well V‑bottom plate; keep on ice.
Prepare 50 µL of single‑step antibody cocktail per well (Table 8; e.g., FcγRIV‑9E9 1:400, BUV737‑CD3ε 1:200, etc.).
Add cocktail, incubate 20 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Top up with 100 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Resuspend in 160 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge again (700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C), discard supernatant.
Resuspend final pellet in 50 µL FACS buffer, keep on ice.
Add 100 µL DAPI working solution before acquisition.

steps.title: Stain differentiation cultures – two‑step
steps.instruction: Perform primary staining followed by secondary staining on DC culture cells (Tables 6 and 7).

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge cells 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend to 1 × 10^6 cells / mL in FACS buffer.
Aliquot 100 µL per well, keep on ice.
Prepare 50 µL primary antibody cocktail per well (Table 6).
Add primary cocktail, incubate 20 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Top up with 100 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Resuspend in 160 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge again (700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C), discard supernatant.
Prepare 50 µL secondary antibody cocktail per well (Table 7).
Add secondary cocktail, incubate 20 min at 4 °C in the dark (check for aggregates).
Top up with 100 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Resuspend in 160 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Resuspend final pellet in 50 µL FACS buffer, keep on ice.
Add 100 µL DAPI working solution before acquisition.

steps.title: Stain cells for DC subset sorting
steps.instruction: Label bone‑marrow‑derived DC cultures with the sorting antibody cocktail (Table 9) under sterile conditions.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge cells 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL ice‑cold sort buffer, then bring volume to 10 mL with sort buffer.
Prepare the sorting antibody cocktail (Table 9) using sterile reagents; keep cells on ice while preparing.
Resuspend cells in the cocktail to achieve 2.5 × 10^6 cells per 100 µL.
Incubate 20 min at 4 °C in the dark; briefly vortex at 10 min to ensure homogeneity.
Top up to 10 mL ice‑cold sort buffer, vortex, centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C.
Discard supernatant, cap tube, spin again briefly at 700 × g and stop; remove residual supernatant with a pipette.
Resuspend in 1 mL ice‑cold sort buffer, top up to 10 mL, vortex, centrifuge 700 × g, 5 min, 4 °C.
Discard supernatant, cap, spin again at 700 × g, stop, remove residual supernatant.
Resuspend final pellet in 200 µL ice‑cold sort buffer and keep on ice until sorting.
